source.original_title: 05/12/2026 - Jacob Gaines & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/12/2026 - Jacob Gaines & Farooq Bey KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Closed

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Prospect at 00:17:14: 'yeah, I spoke with Kim earlier today.' Also 00:31:00: 'I was planning on joining this one today, and then I got a call from Kim, so this started this conversation with the 1-on-1 thing.' And 00:43:40: 'I thought Kim was in London too.'

prospect.name: Jacob Gaines
prospect.occupation: Life coach and somatic breathwork facilitator, building the practice; caregiving job as the current day job. Recently completed a somatic breathwork facilitation certification and is finishing his practicum.
prospect.family_status: Partner of two and a half years; no children mentioned
prospect.training_background: Lifelong athlete. Weights, calisthenics, resistance bands, gymnastic rings, football. Used kettlebells incidentally when playing football but has never done a targeted functional kettlebell programme. Surfs, hikes, practises kung fu and martial arts. Does little dedicated cardio beyond walking. Rates himself seven out of ten against his athletic potential. Discovered Trevor's content about five days before the call.

signals: Explicitly has no problem to solve — 'I would say I actually have great health and fitness. I'm just always looking to upgrade and try new things... there's not really any big pain points'
Good-to-great stated almost as a philosophy — 'I'm at peace where I am now, and I'm just excited to up-level forever. Like, I'm just a student of life, and I'm always reaching for my potential'
No pain, no injuries, self-rated seven out of ten and wanting the ten

Diverges from the definition on 'successful' and on price: he is building a coaching practice while working a caregiving day job, and ruled out the coaching tier before hearing its price — 'investing in one-on-one coaching may not be the move right now'

goals.text: Learn targeted functional kettlebell training, a style he has never done — 'that style of training just excites me and I'm just ready to change it up'
Keep building muscle while improving mobility
Get cardiovascular work in a way he enjoys — 'I don't like cardio much... this seems like a more fun way to get my cardio in'
More energy and vitality entering his thirties — 'I want to feel good, not just look good, feel open and flexible'
Train outdoors rather than in a gym — 'kind of done with being in the gym and fluorescent lighting. I want to train in the sun and be barefoot in the grass'
Build discipline that ripples into the rest of his life and his coaching business
Carry more presence and credibility as a coach — 'when someone is fit and capable, and they look solid, it sends a message that they're in control of themselves'
Train his core as an integrated part of movement rather than in isolation
Learn mace training as well as kettlebells

pains.text: Does little dedicated cardio and knows it is a gap — 'the cardio is something that I don't do a lot of. And that's a big piece that I want to have in my life'
Has never trained core consistently — 'something I haven't been consistent with in the past is consistently hitting core'
Bored of conventional gym training and wants a change of modality
Building a coaching practice while holding a caregiving day job, which constrains discretionary spend — 'investing in one-on-one coaching may not be the move right now'

objections.raw_quote: yeah, what do you get from the community? Because, yeah, investing in one-on-one coaching may not be the move right now, and I just want to save us time if that's where the call is going. I want to see if I can get everything I need getting into credible training, starting off with that. Yep. I'm open to hearing, too, what the one-on-one looks like.
objections.rep_response: Conceded immediately rather than isolating or presenting. Abandoned the pillar presentation midway, screen-shared Primal University, and told him coaching probably would not serve him: 'One-on-one coaching from the sounds of it, I'm not sure if it will. This, on the other hand, probably is.' The coaching price was never stated, despite the prospect explicitly saying he was open to hearing about it.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Primal University purchased at $200/month. No coaching tier was ever quoted.

evidence: Payment completed and confirmed live on the call — 'Well, I joined. It says like I got a receipt, so I'm good to go' and earlier 'It's loading' after being walked into the Skool app
Explicit agreement: 'Yeah, I mean, I was, yeah, I was gonna, I'm planning on joining today, so I might as well'
Rep onboarded him into Skool live and confirmed access
Critical caveat for any close-rate rollup: what closed was Primal University at $200/month, NOT the coaching programme. The $6,000 and $9,000 tiers were never presented or priced on this call.

Counter-evidence on attribution: he had already decided to buy this product before the call existed — 'I was planning on joining this one today, and then I got a call from Kim, so this started this conversation with the 1-on-1 thing. But I was already ready to go to sign up with this.' The call generated no incremental revenue.
outcome.next_step: Access Primal University via the Skool app; rep advised buying a 20 lb and a 35 lb kettlebell to start. Separately, the rep agreed to receive a free breathwork session from the prospect and to exchange WhatsApp details for it.

notable.note: The most interesting commercial finding in the batch is not what was sold but what the sale cost. The prospect had already decided to buy Primal University at $200 before the call — 'I was already ready to go to sign up with this' — and was pulled into a one-to-one closer call by the setter. A 28-minute closer conversation produced revenue that was already coming. Meanwhile the coaching offer was never presented, even though he said outright, 'I'm open to hearing, too, what the one-on-one looks like.' The rep also abandoned the three-pillar presentation halfway: pillars two and three were never delivered and the prospect had to ask 'What were the other two pillars?', receiving a one-sentence answer. Clinically this is the cleanest call in the batch — no conditions, no pain, no injuries, and none missed. At the end the rep accepted a free breathwork session from the customer for the customer's certification practicum and moved the relationship to WhatsApp. This call shares a file with an entirely separate earlier call with a prospect named Dylan.

quality.notes: Two unrelated calls share this file; Jacob's begins at 00:16:24 after the rep is heard phoning him. Labels invert constantly within it — the rep's own questions 'How can we potentially help you?', 'Why?' and 'how old are you' appear under Jacob's label, and Jacob's answers under the rep's. The exchange from 00:26:31 to 00:26:36 is fully inverted. Connection dropped repeatedly in the second half and both parties acknowledge it, producing several garbled passages. Roles resolved from content throughout.
